need_scores.description: Need for a larger health insurance cover to protect against high hospitalization costs.
need_scores.customer_friendly_description: A higher cover can help reduce out-of-pocket expenses during major hospitalization.
need_scores.advisor_explanation: Important where medical costs, family size, lifestyle, income level, or city of residence justify higher protection.
need_scores.risk_caution: Higher sum insured may increase premium. Affordability should be checked.
need_scores.compliance_note: Recommendation should be based on customer affordability and documented protection need.

adjustments.reason: Family responsibilities increase the need for stronger health protection.
adjustments.customer_friendly_reason: A higher cover can be useful as your family responsibilities grow.

adjustments.reason: Treatment costs are generally higher in metro cities.
adjustments.customer_friendly_reason: Hospitals in metro cities can be expensive, so a higher cover may be useful.

adjustments.reason: Higher income can support stronger cover and better hospital choice.
adjustments.customer_friendly_reason: Your income may support a higher cover for better protection.

adjustments.reason: Existing cover may be insufficient for major hospitalization.
adjustments.customer_friendly_reason: Your current cover may not be enough for large medical bills.

need_scores.description: Need for shorter waiting periods for pre-existing disease, specified disease, maternity, or initial coverage.
need_scores.customer_friendly_description: Lower waiting periods can help you access certain benefits sooner.
need_scores.advisor_explanation: Important for customers with existing health conditions, family planning needs, or urgency around coverage usability.
need_scores.risk_caution: Waiting period comparison must be based on exact policy wording and benefit context.
need_scores.compliance_note: Do not claim coverage is immediately available unless explicitly supported by evidence.

adjustments.reason: Waiting periods matter because maternity and some disease benefits may not be immediately available.
adjustments.customer_friendly_reason: Lower waiting periods may help you use important benefits sooner.

adjustments.reason: Lower waiting periods improve usability of incremental protection.
adjustments.customer_friendly_reason: Lower waiting periods may make added coverage useful sooner.

need_scores.description: Need for flexible room rent eligibility or fewer room category restrictions.
need_scores.customer_friendly_description: Room rent flexibility may help you choose better hospital rooms without proportionate deductions.
need_scores.advisor_explanation: Important in metro cities and higher-cost hospitals where room category can affect total claim payout.
need_scores.risk_caution: Room rent limits may trigger proportionate deductions depending on policy terms.
need_scores.compliance_note: Room rent claims impact should be explained carefully and evidence-backed.

adjustments.reason: Family hospitalization in metro or private hospitals can make room rent flexibility useful.
adjustments.customer_friendly_reason: Room rent flexibility can help avoid restrictions during hospitalization.

adjustments.reason: Room costs are generally higher in metro hospitals.
adjustments.customer_friendly_reason: Room rent flexibility can help reduce restrictions during hospitalization.

adjustments.reason: Customer may prefer better room category and hospital flexibility.
adjustments.customer_friendly_reason: Room rent flexibility can help you choose better hospital accommodation.

need_scores.description: Need for maternity, delivery, and newborn-related benefits.
need_scores.customer_friendly_description: Useful if you are planning a family or may need maternity and newborn-related support.
need_scores.advisor_explanation: Highly relevant for married couples planning children. Waiting periods and benefit limits must be checked carefully.
need_scores.risk_caution: Maternity benefits usually have waiting periods, sub-limits, and eligibility conditions.
need_scores.compliance_note: Do not imply immediate maternity coverage unless waiting period and conditions are verified.

adjustments.reason: Maternity and newborn benefits become highly relevant for family planning.
adjustments.customer_friendly_reason: If you are planning a family, maternity and newborn-related benefits become important.

need_scores.description: Need to avoid mandatory co-payment during claims.
need_scores.customer_friendly_description: A plan with no or lower co-pay may reduce your share of claim expenses.
need_scores.advisor_explanation: Especially important for senior citizens, customers with higher claim probability, or customers who want predictable out-of-pocket cost.
need_scores.risk_caution: Co-pay may vary by age, zone, claim type, room category, or network rules.
need_scores.compliance_note: Co-pay interpretation must be verified against policy wording.

adjustments.customer_friendly_reason: Lower or no co-pay can reduce your share of claim expenses.

adjustments.reason: Customer may prefer lower out-of-pocket exposure during claims.
adjustments.customer_friendly_reason: Avoiding co-pay can reduce claim-time expenses.

need_scores.description: Need for wellness, preventive health, health rewards, or wellness-linked benefits.
need_scores.customer_friendly_description: Wellness benefits may reward healthy behavior or support preventive care.
need_scores.advisor_explanation: Useful for health-conscious customers and families interested in preventive care and long-term engagement.
need_scores.risk_caution: Wellness benefits should not be treated as a substitute for core hospitalization coverage.
need_scores.compliance_note: Wellness rewards and discounts should be explained as per policy terms.

adjustments.reason: Preventive care and wellness benefits are useful for young families.
adjustments.customer_friendly_reason: Wellness benefits may support preventive health for the family.
